title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 28
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 28: the drunkards of Ephraim, the covenant with death, and the precious cornerstone laid in Zion.

questions.text: To whom is the first woe of this chapter addressed?
questions.explanation: The woe is to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower of his glorious beauty.

answers.text: The scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem
The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim
The kings of the earth and all their armies
The priests and the prophets of Samaria

questions.text: To what is the fading flower of Ephraim's glorious beauty compared?
questions.explanation: It is like the first-ripe fig before the summer, which someone picks and eats as soon as he sees it.

answers.text: A rose of the desert withering in the heat
An olive branch broken off and withered away
A cluster of grapes left after the vintage is done
The first-ripe fig, picked and eaten as soon as seen

questions.text: What will Yahweh of Armies become to the residue of his people in that day?
questions.explanation: In that day Yahweh of Armies will become a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the residue of his people.

answers.text: A crown of glory and a diadem of beauty
A devouring and consuming fire
A strong tower and a high fortress
A shepherd and a guide to his flock

questions.text: What do the priest and the prophet do, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink; they err in vision and stumble in judgment.

answers.text: They teach the people knowledge
They fast and pray for the city
They reel with strong drink and err in vision
They flee to Egypt for refuge

questions.text: How is Yahweh's word described to those who would not hear?
questions.explanation: His word will be to them precept on precept, line on line, here a little, there a little, that they may go, fall backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.

answers.text: A hammer that breaks the hardest rock in pieces
Precept on precept, line on line, here a little, there a little
A sealed book that neither wise nor simple can read
A sharp two-edged sword that strikes the nations

questions.text: With what do the scoffers who rule in Jerusalem say they have made a covenant?
questions.explanation: The rulers say, "We have made a covenant with death, and we are in agreement with Sheol," trusting that the overflowing scourge will not come to them.

answers.text: With death, and an agreement with Sheol
With Egypt, and an agreement with Pharaoh
With Assyria, and an agreement with its king
With the sea, and an agreement with the deep

questions.text: What does the Lord Yahweh say he lays in Zion for a foundation?
questions.explanation: He says, "Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation."

answers.text: A measuring line of justice stretched over the city
A throne of righteousness that stands forever
An altar built of twelve unhewn stones
A tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation

questions.text: What will sweep away the refuge of lies?
questions.explanation: Yahweh will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line; the hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters will overflow the hiding place.

answers.text: The east wind
The overflowing stream
The hail
The devouring fire

questions.text: What picture shows that the scoffers' refuge is inadequate?
questions.explanation: The bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.

answers.text: A bed too short and a blanket too narrow
A wall ready to fall
A broken cistern that holds no water
A house built on the sand

questions.text: How is the dill beaten out at threshing time?
questions.explanation: The dill is not threshed with a sharp instrument but is beaten out with a stick, and the cumin with a rod.

answers.text: With a cart wheel
With a stick
With the feet of oxen
With a sharp instrument
